children: Global stocks sold off and Treasurys strengthened as investor confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of cracking.

Nasdaq futures dropped 1.7%, extending sharp falls from the last session. S&P 500 futures fell 0.85%, while contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.2%. Major U.S. indexes are on track for their worst week since the announcement of President Trump's so-called Liberation Day tariffs upended global trade in April 2025.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to stem heavy selling across global stocks. Chip makers, tech giants and cloud-computing stocks weakened in U.S. premarket trade after heavy selling across Asian tech names. The memory chip-dominated Kospi closed 5.2% lower, while Japan's Nikkei also fell more than 5%. Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.2%, bringing its weekly loss to 17.5%--its worst week since 1990.

The selling bled to European stocks, too. ASML, the continent's most valuable stock, tumbled by more than 6% as a basket of the continent's tech stocks traded 4% lower. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 was 1.7% lower.

"I think the market seriously underestimated just how much liquidity Anthropic's IPO would require," said NinjaTrader economist Tracy Shuchart in a post on X. "The question isn't whether investors want exposure to AI. It's whether the market has sufficient liquidity to absorb this much supply without forcing liquidation elsewhere."

The gloominess in stock market sentiment comes despite fresh declines for oil. Benchmark Brent crude contracts dropped around 0.3% to $91.70 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts fell 0.7% to trade around $82.60 a barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that oil shipments through major Middle Eastern shipping routes increased 19% in the third quarter.

Lower oil prices and an investor flight to safety combined to strengthen Treasurys. Ten-year yields fell back below 5.000%, while two-year yields dropped 8.7 basis points to 4.690%. Thirty-year yields fell 5.3 basis points to trade around 5.340%.

Metals prices continued to sell off, with gold tumbling over 3% to $3,570 a troy ounce. Silver contracts fell close to 5%. The dollar held near multimonth highs, while bitcoin hovered around lows not seen since the beginning of July, trading at $61,530.
For the day ahead, macro watchers will look to Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November, and to Federal Reserve speakers including Christopher Waller.
